Q1_ICSA_lookahead.evidence_text: ICSA raw is dated 2020-03-14, forward-filled immediately, enters the 28-day rolling average, and is exposed as us_initial_claims_4w_avg_lag1 from 2020-03-15 / first KR panel date 2020-03-16, before the following-Thursday release is KR next-open observable.

Q2_CFNAI_lookahead.evidence_text: CFNAI -18.28 is dated 2020-04-01, forward-filled by observation date, and exposed as us_cfnai_lag1 from 2020-04-02, while the March 2020 reading was not release-observable until about 2020-04-23 ET / 2020-04-24 KR next open.

Q3_STLFSI4_lookahead.evidence_text: STLFSI4 is forward-filled then shifted one row. A Friday value is first available to KR trading on the next Korean trading day after its same-Friday noon ET release, so shift(1L) is sufficient for KR next_open.

Q4_T10Y2Y_lookahead.evidence_text: T10Y2Y is daily, forward-filled, then shifted one calendar row. Given after-US-close / early-KST availability, the t observation is not used until t+1 KR date, so no lookahead is introduced by this code.

Q5_BBVA_Markets_via_ICSA.evidence_text: Init_Claims is LOCF-filled by FRED observation date, differenced, z-scored, included in bbva_market_z and bbva_macro_composite, then lagged only one row. The Saturday-dated claims release therefore leaks into BBVA market/composite features before Thursday release visibility.

Q6_BBVA_Sovereign_BBB_HY.evidence_text: BBB_Spread and HY_Spread are daily inputs, transformed using same-row differences/z-scores and exposed only through bbva_sovereign_z_lag1. No source-code evidence of future-dated publication lag is present for these daily spread fields.

Q7_unused_monthly_ffill.evidence_text: US_M2, US_CPI, US_IndProd, and UMich_Sentiment are LOCF-filled but are not referenced in the market, sovereign, transmission, or composite z-score computations. In current A6 output they are discarded and benign.

Q8_already_lag1_base_naming.evidence_text: The base panel aliases already-lagged A3/A5/A6 features under base names, and enhanced lag1/lag5/lag21 applies another shift. These are effectively lag2/lag6/lag22 versus raw signal time; naming is relative to the base panel and can be misleading, but this is not future leakage.

Q9_rolling_window_align_right.evidence_text: Rolling mean/std use align='right' on base features. At panel row t the window uses base rows [t-w+1, t], which for already-lag1 bases corresponds to true signal times ending at t-1. The rolling operation adds no new lookahead.

Q10_intx_product_safety.evidence_text: Interactions multiply same-date base features. If both inputs are lag1-observable, the product is also lag1-observable. The operation itself is causal, though interactions using BBVA inputs inherit the source-level ICSA leak confirmed in Q5.

Q11_ECOS_date_shift_semantics.evidence_text: ffill_monthly copies the monthly series and shifts Date forward by pub_lag_days before any rolling fill. This represents the first availability date as original Date + publication lag.

Q12_rolling_join_semantics.evidence_text: series_shifted[panel, roll=TRUE] returns one row per panel date and selects the latest shifted series Date <= panel Date. That is equivalent to using only values already published by the panel date.

Q13_ECOS_monthly_M2_IP_CPI_safety.evidence_text: Monthly TIME is parsed to the first day of the month, then M2/CPI are shifted +35 days and IP +50 days before rolling fill. For Date=2020-02-01, code visibility starts at 2020-03-07 calendar date, which is conservative under the stated Jan-reading / Feb-release convention.

Q14_inst_breadth_lag_correctness.evidence_text: Inst breadth is extracted by trade Date, 5d/20d averages explicitly use align='right', and all resulting features are shifted by 1 row. For KRX 18:10 same-day publication, this is PIT-correct for next KR open.

Q15_standardize_train_only.evidence_text: col_med, mean, and std are all computed from X_work[train_mask]. The resulting train-only constants are then applied to the full matrix, including OOS, without using OOS statistics.

Q16_walk_forward_stationarity.evidence_text: A fixed 1995-01-01 to 2009-12-31 train_mask used to standardize 2010-2026 OOS uses only past training data. This is not a PIT violation; it is a stationarity/distribution-drift concern.

Q17_sequence_padding_causal.evidence_text: sliding_window_view builds each sequence from contiguous rows ending at the aligned date index, and dates_seq starts at dates[SEQ_LEN-1:]. No future rows beyond the sequence end are included.

Q18_y_seq_target_alignment.evidence_text: y_seq = y[seq_len - 1:] aligns each sequence ending at row t with y[t]. Given y is already a forward label such as q15/q126, the sequence code preserves the intended target alignment.

additional_issues_found.description: FRED fetch uses the latest fredgraph.csv endpoint with no realtime/vintage/as-of parameters. For revised FRED series, historical rows in fred_us_macro_daily.csv can contain post-date revisions, which is a separate current-vintage PIT risk beyond the publication-lag bugs.
